Thanks Michael — I pulled logs and cross-referenced billing tokens. Quick summary: 3 separate billing tokens (tok_xxxA, tok_xxxB, tok_xxxC) tied to three distinct teams but share two things: 1) recurring requests originate from the same /24 IP block (likely a contractor or NATed office) and 2) the Device-Fingerprint header is identical in 18 of 22 top-ups.

I don't see obvious bot signatures (ratelimits respected, human timing), but the Device-Fingerprint reuse is suspicious — usually different teams use different environments. There are also four accounts created in a 36-hour window that received small pilot credits then immediately requested additional top-ups.

Suggested next steps:
- Freeze further credit issuance for the tokens flagged while we confirm with the customer contact.
- Ask Fraud Ops to run a deeper device fingerprint analysis (I can open a ticket).

I attached a short CSV of correlated indicators.

Ethan — copying our account team and risk lead. We detected multiple evaluation/top-up credit requests tied to Glacier AI over the past three weeks under tokens tok_xxxA/B/C. Two quick asks so we can process requests safely:

1) Can you confirm which internal teams are running pilots and the expected seat counts for each? If different business units are running independent pilots please share the list of point people and the intended usage window.
2) If these are distinct pilots, can you provide a purchase order or procurement note that authorizes separate top-ups?

Per our risk policy we have temporarily put a hold on additional credits for the flagged tokens while we confirm. This is standard — if you can share the PO or a short email from the business owner confirming the pilots we'll unblock.

If needed, we can set up a 30-minute sync today to expedite. Also linking our fraud policy for reference: https://redwood.app/docs/fraud-playbook#trial-credit-policies

Thanks,

Hi Michael — thanks for the flag and sorry for the confusion. Quick context: we spun up three independent evaluation projects across Research, Product, and Ops while coordinating with different vendors. That split the workstreams and requestors. I attached a consolidated PO and a short note from each internal owner confirming their pilot scope.

We did rely on a third-party consultant to do initial provisioning, which explains the shared IP. That consultant consolidated requests on our behalf and didn't provide clear provenance for each top-up — that's my oversight. We've terminated the consultant's provisioning tokens and pushed for centralized procurement going forward.

Next steps from our side:
- I've uploaded a single master PO to DocuSign to adjust terms and centralize billing (https://app.docusign.com/some-doc-id/GL-2381-updated-terms).
